newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-French insurer GAN makes first half loss.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French insurer GAN makes first half loss.

text.p: French state insurer GAN, hit by property losses, reported on Wednesday a first-half loss of nearly one billion francs ($193 million) and warned it might need a further state cash injection before being privatised.

The insurer, which has already generated a flood of red ink, reported its net consolidated loss for the six months to end June ballooned to 965 million francs from a loss of 387 million francs a year earlier.
Chairman Jean-Jacques Bonnaud, who in April forecast the insurer would break even this year, warned it would post a full-year loss but "not necessarily double" the sum reported for the first half.
Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN), France's third largest insurer, made a loss of 1.8 billion francs in 1995. The previous year it recorded a loss of 5.3 billion francs.
Losses by its real estate banking activities totalling 1.79 billion francs were mainly behind the first-half loss and Bonnaud warned they could hit the same level in the second half.
The group, which has already received 2.8 billion francs of state money, said it was studying ways to reinforce shareholder funds ahead of its planned privatisation.
Bonnaud said GAN's sale was still a "realistic possibility (for 1997) if we can do it with the support of our state shareholder".
He would not say how much the insurer might need from the state to prepare it for sale. But he said the insurer needed to put its property problems behind it before it could be sold.

He said GAN was studying stepping up property disposals and could carry out a large sale of distressed real estate similar to operations carried out by other French financial institutions seeking to clean up their real estate accounts.
Such a sale would require further property provisions for losses on the disposals. These provisions would have to be compensated by the state, he said.
He said he also expected the state would have to compensate GAN for any loss suffered on the sale of 67 percent of its banking arm CIC, now in process of privatisation.

The government is considering "expressions of interest" in CIC. But strict conditions on the sale are said to have lessened appetite for it and there are reports that offers by banks BNP and Societe Generale SOCG.PA are considerably below the 14.6 billion franc ($2.8 billion) value placed on it.

GAN's banking property arm Union Industrielle de Credit, a longstanding source of problems, made a negative contribution of 799 million francs to group results. Plans for an 800 million recapitalisation of the unit were announced last summer.

But its core insurance business made a profit of 464 million francs after slashing the losses in non-life insurance in France and a big improvement in underlying profits from its French life assurance business. "This is a very satisfying development," Bonnaud said.
GAN's French life assurance business generated a profit of 425 million francs versus 627 but the figure last time round had been inflated by one-off gains of 432 million francs.
